question.text: The speed of a swimmer is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>km</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> in still water. If the swimmer makes his strokes normal to the flow of river of width <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>km</mi></math>, he reaches a point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>750</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> down the stream on the opposite bank. The speed of the river water is ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>km</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>.

solution.text:
Let vr be velocity of river and vm be velocity of man.

Time taken by man to cross the river of width =1000 m is t=14 h.

Now, drift x=vr×t

⇒0.750=vr×14⇒vr=3 km h-1
